stories.headline: Brown Says A Word, Scott Says Nothing
stories.deck: Scott, owned by test3331, gets a mention in a Celtic-Rangers preview that carries no draft weight.
stories.body:
Scott Brown holds forth on Sunday's derby, and somewhere in the copy sits the name test3331 will care about. Scott is on those rolls, and a big Old Firm afternoon is the sort that reads across to a fantasy owner watching from a distance.

What the wire gives is a preview and a former captain's verdict, no more. No line-up, no minutes, no fitness note attached to Scott. test3331 knows the fixture is coming and knows nothing beyond it, and neither do we.

stories.headline: Haaland Holds The Balance For 123
stories.deck: Man City v Sunderland Sunday, test4's front three of Foden, Isidor and Cherki against 123's Haaland with a 6-26 tie already lopsided.
stories.body:
The 6-26 gap is real, but ninety minutes here can widen it or start the climb back. test4 loads this fixture: Foden, E.Le Fée, Isidor and Cherki all in the same match, four men chasing the twenty-point hole that 123 opened up. Against them 123 leans on Reinildo, Hume and above all Haaland, the one man who can turn a lopsided tie into a rout in a single afternoon.

The smaller duel carries its own weight. test31, six points back on testf, sends Ballard alone into a fixture where testf answer with Rúben, N.Angulo and Xhaka. One defender against three, the two-point chase now a six-point one, and testf's spread of men leaving Ballard to do the work by himself. Guéhi and Semenyo for test1, Roefs for test211, Ndiaye for test3 all watch on with no tie riding on them here.

stories.headline: On The South Coast, Three Ties Hang
stories.deck: Bournemouth v Liverpool carries three open duels: test1's Gravenberch and Wirtz meet test2's Isak, test211's Gakpo meets test3331's Cook and Scott, test31's Munoz meets testf's Evanilson and Tavernier.
stories.body:
Ninety minutes on the south coast, three ties held in the balance, and men on both sides of every one. test1 trail test2 by five and send Gravenberch and Wirtz out against a single visiting name, Isak. One haul either way and the margin reads differently by mid-afternoon.

test211 sit twelve back on test3331 and lean on Gakpo alone, with Cook and Scott stood the other way. test31 chase testf by four with Munoz to answer Evanilson and Tavernier, testf's attacking pair now asked to do what their defenders have been doing. Szoboszlai and Petrović are in it too, for test31121, with no duel to swing but points to take out of the room.

stories.headline: Cottagers Host United, Ties Held Hostage
stories.deck: Fulham v Man Utd puts four open head-to-heads on the line, Cunha and B.Fernandes leading the men split across it.
stories.body:
Four ties come to this fixture unresolved and every one has a man on each side of it. test2 leads test1 16-11, and the split is clean: Dalot for test1, Cunha for test2. The wider gulf is test4's, six against 123's twenty-six, with Mbeumo carrying the deficit and B.Fernandes standing for the side already clear.

Elsewhere the margins are tighter. test3, with Maguire and Gonzalo, trails test31121 and Berge by two. test211 hold King and Castagne against Leno for test3331, six adrift of eighteen. Bobb is in it too, no duel to his name, watching for test31 as the league's top scorers chase testf's lead. Ninety minutes, four ledgers, and nobody knows yet which way any of them tips.

stories.headline: Palace Guard Bogle Eyes The Elland Lot
stories.deck: Leeds v Palace sits inside two open ties, with Calvert-Lewin against Trafford and Rodon and Justin against Stach over the same ninety
stories.body:
Two ties ride on one afternoon. test1 trail test2 by five, and the whole of it narrows to Leeds and Palace: Calvert-Lewin leading the line for test1, Trafford between the sticks for test2. A forward's afternoon against a goalkeeper's clean sheet, and neither can have both.

Deeper in the hole sit test4, twenty short of 123 at six against twenty-six, with Rodon and Justin on one side of this match and Stach on the other. A twenty-point tie does not close on one fixture, but a defensive return here and a midfield blank there is where it starts. Ampadu, Bogle and Aaronson all feature too, men in the ninety minutes with no duel to carry.

stories.headline: Gvardiol Backs Himself At Left-Back
stories.deck: test31121's Gvardiol reported returning to his best at left-back for City after an injury-hit spell
stories.body:
The wire has Josko Gvardiol trending back towards his best, the left-sided defender central to a strong City start after injury wrecked the back end of his last campaign. For test31121, the reading is simple enough: a defender on the rolls looks fit and looks trusted.

No return date is attached because none is needed here. He is playing, and that is the point. test31121's back line has carried enough uncertainty this season without one of its better names in doubt.

stories.headline: Barry Good Return For test31
stories.deck: Barry's goal for Everton over 10-man Ipswich lands in test31's column.
stories.body:
Everton go unbeaten again, fifth in the table, and Thierno Barry supplies the goal that settles it against ten men. For test31 that is the return, and it lands with testf's two-point lead still to be answered.

One strike, one owner. test31 needed the front men to fire in that chase, and Barry is the one who has.

stories.headline: Suzuki Fills The Gap For test4
stories.deck: Suzuki keeps goal in Villa's first win; Martinez, owned by test3331, watches on.
stories.body:
The Villa goal has changed hands, and so has the draft value in it. Zion Suzuki, on test4's rolls, kept a clean sheet as Villa took their first league win of the season at Tottenham. For a manager already leaning on his newest men to close a hole, a goalkeeper delivering in the fixture is the answer test4 needed.

For test3331 it is the other side of the same coin. Emiliano Martinez, still owned here, no longer holds the position, and the wire does not say when or whether that changes. What is known is that the return came from the man in the sticks, and the man in the sticks belongs to somebody else.

stories.headline: Suzuki Motors test4 Forward
stories.deck: test4's Suzuki keeps goal in Villa's 3-2 win at Spurs, a plus for test4 against 123
stories.body:
Zion Suzuki kept goal in Villa's 3-2 win at Tottenham, and Emery singled him out afterwards. He is test4's man, and test4 is the one manager who needs a name to answer this week.

A winning goalkeeper who draws his manager's praise is the return test4 was chasing against 123. What the line reads is not yet ours to print, only that Suzuki was on the right side of a five-goal match and named for it.

stories.headline: Pedro Out, test211 Short Up Front
stories.deck: João Pedro, owned by test211, ruled out through injury with no return date given
stories.body:
João Pedro is out injured, and test211 lose the forward without a line on how long. The wire has Chelsea unable to score without him, which is the part that matters here: a striker on the treatment table is a striker returning nothing until he is fit.

No timeframe has been given, so none is offered. test211's defenders have already been doing the heavy lifting week to week, and now they do it a man light at the sharp end.

stories.headline: Gabriel Blows In A Catalan Wind
stories.deck: test31121's teenager JJ Gabriel travels to Barcelona as Europe's biggest clubs chase his signature.
stories.body:
The clubs circling JJ Gabriel are not test31121's problem yet, but they are test31121's asset. The 15-year-old has travelled to Barcelona while the biggest names in Europe queue for a signature, and the manager who holds him on this league's rolls watches the same reports as the rest of us.

Nothing has changed on paper. Gabriel is still test31121's, no minutes attach to any of it, and there is nothing to act on. But a squad that has already given its owner a flat midfield and a selection headache now has a name whose next move belongs to somebody else entirely.

stories.headline: Two Deals, No Rush, Same Old Story
stories.deck: Only two moves in the window, nobody churning, Raya still unclaimed.
stories.body:
Two deals in the window. Call it what it is: a quiet week, quieter than the last if that were possible, and the last was already a morgue.

test4 did their one piece of business the honest way, one in and one out, the only manager in the league to trade rather than merely add. test31 and testf each took a single name and gave up nothing. That is the whole of it. Nobody is churning, nobody is turning over a squad, and the waiver wire has the traffic of a Sunday morning.

David Raya remains where he was left. Signed in hope, dropped without ceremony, survived by a bench spot. The league has walked past him five times now and shows no sign of stooping.

Which is the trend, such as it is: the men the league keeps passing around are the men nobody wants twice. Two deals do not make a market.

quiz.q: How many deals went through the window this week?
Which manager was the only one to move a player out?
Which two managers added a player without dropping one?

stories.headline: test1 shades it as test4 draws blanks
stories.deck: test1 beat test4 38-11, Calvert-Lewin's eight the top score
stories.body:
Nothing worked for test4 and nothing came close. Eleven points across six men, not one of them past three, and the whole afternoon summed up by Gray's three at the top of the pile. Mbeumo two, Suzuki two, Justin two, N.Williams two, Cherki one. A ceiling that low loses to most totals and lost to this one by 27.

test1 needed no heroics and got a spread anyway. Calvert-Lewin's eight led it, Guéhi and Saka each returned six from opposite ends of the pitch, and Palmer's five kept the middle ticking over. Kelleher and Wirtz added three apiece and the thing was settled long before the maths got interesting.

What will gnaw at test4 is the absence of a single haul to hang the week on. Everyone contributed a little; nobody contributed enough. When your best forward returns two, the arithmetic is unkind before you start.

stories.headline: Dunk done: test3 sinks test2
stories.deck: test3 beat test2 46-21, Dunk's twelve from the back the top score
stories.body:
A defender fronted this one. Dunk's twelve settled it long before the forwards were counted, and Calafiori's six behind him meant test3 took eighteen from two men filed in defence. Emersonn's nine gave the top of the sheet the weight the back of it did not need.

Pickford's six for the clean sheet and Gibbs-White's five rounded a total that never looked like slipping. Only Gonzalo, on two, kept quiet.

test2 had nothing to answer with. Rice's six was the best of it and everything after fell away, Giles on four, Trafford on three from goal, Cunha and Isak on two apiece. Two forwards for four points is the line that will gnaw at him.

Twenty-five is a hammering, and it was built where test2 will least have expected it, in the two defensive slots that carried eighteen on their own.

stories.headline: Groß national product carries 123 39
stories.deck: 123 39 edge test211 40-39, Groß's 14 the top score
stories.body:
Fourteen from Groß did the settling. The midfielder was the biggest number on either side, and 123 39 needed every point of him, because behind that the returns thinned fast. Schade added ten up front, Haaland six, and a one-point win was built on the pair at the top and little else.

The floor is where 123 39 will look with relief. Stach three, B.Fernandes two, Neto two. Slim contributions, but in a margin of one they all counted.

test211 lost this by a single point and the defence is what will gnaw. Bogle led the side with twelve, Castagne added six, Aina two, three defenders returning and still not enough. João Pedro's nine up front was honest work with nobody alongside him, King and Enciso managing two apiece. One more point anywhere and the tie flips.

stories.headline: Verbruggen's clean sheet keeps test31 dry
stories.deck: test31 beats test31121 34-31, Verbruggen's eight and Belloumi's nine decisive
stories.body:
Two nines split this tie down the middle, and it was the man behind them who tipped it. Verbruggen's clean sheet and eight points gave test31 a base test31121 could not match, and Belloumi's nine up top matched Kostoulas blow for blow. Mykolenko's six from the back did the rest of the settling.

test31121 will point at the top of the sheet and rightly so: Kostoulas returned nine, the equal of anything test31 had. But behind him the picture thinned fast. Ampadu and Gabriel managed five apiece and the midfield trio of Berge, Ødegaard and Szoboszlai returned three each, and three points from a midfielder is not the return a captaincy expects.

The margin was three, which is exactly the gap between test31's goalkeeper and test31121's not having one that scored. Belloumi and Kostoulas cancelled; Verbruggen did not. That is the tie.

stories.headline: De Cuyper leads, test3331 left counting
stories.deck: testf beat test3331 46-19, De Cuyper's nine the top score of the tie
stories.body:
testf carried this on defenders. De Cuyper's nine led it, with Rúben and Tarkowski both on six and a clean sheet's worth of coverage across the back. Add Tavernier's six in midfield and Rogers and Evanilson up top, and testf had six men returning and nobody dragging.

test3331's total tells the other story. Nineteen from six players, and Leno's seven from goal was the only stat line that stood up. Everything in front of him folded.

McBurnie's four was the best of the outfield returns, and that is the number test3331 will chew on. Barkley and Scott managed two apiece, Ajer and Lewis-Potter one each. Six starters, five of them in single figures, against a testf side that never dropped below five. Twenty-seven is a hole no single haul was ever going to fill.

stories.headline: Tuchel's Chaos, test3331's Concern
stories.deck: Tuchel embraces chaos in his England squad; test3331 owns Thomas.
stories.body:
Thomas Tuchel wanted control after the World Cup. Two months on he has named his Nations League squad and settled instead for chaos, a word he now uses without flinching.

For test3331 the interest is narrower and named Thomas, the one asset on the books with a stake in whatever Tuchel decides to embrace. What the England camp does to his minutes, the wire does not say, and neither do we.

stories.headline: Palmer Recalled, test1 On Warning Too
stories.deck: Tuchel recalls Palmer, owned by test1, and Alexander-Arnold, with a warning that players must perform.
stories.body:
Cole Palmer is back in the England fold, and test1 will note the caveat that came with him. Tuchel recalled the midfielder alongside Trent Alexander-Arnold, then made plain that a place in the squad guarantees nothing beyond it. Selection is not the same as trust, and test1 owns a player Tuchel wants to see earn his.

For test3331 there is nothing here to read. Thomas remains theirs, and the recall list did not trouble him one way or the other. Two owners watched the same announcement; only one of them found their name in it.

stories.headline: Benched but not beaten
stories.deck: Team of the week 5-3-3, Groß top with 12, three of the eleven left out by their own managers
stories.body:
Groß is the man of the week and it is not close. A goal, two assists and a clean sheet from midfield is the full ledger, the sort of line that decides a gameweek on its own, and 123 rode it. Everything else here orbits that return.

The back five is the story a manager would rather forget. Davis went for a goal and two assists and watched from his own bench while it happened, and he was not alone: Gvardiol and Yalcouyé, both of test31121, were sat down by the same hand that owned their points. Three men picked for this eleven were deemed surplus by the men who paid for them. Dunk, Bogle and De Cuyper kept their sheets clean and got on the scoresheet besides, but the column belongs to the ones left out.

The middle is thin by design at three, and it earns its keep. Rice supplied an assist and a clean sheet from the base of it, tidy rather than spectacular, and Yalcouyé's goal from midfield forces him in even benched. There was room for one more and no clear case to make it.

Up top the front three did the finishing the shape demands. Belloumi took a brace inside an hour, Kostoulas married a goal and an assist to a clean sheet at the other end, and Calvert-Lewin matched him for output in less time still. Three forwards, three goals, and not a wasted body among them.

Unlucky to miss is Calvert-Lewin's near-twin in the pecking order, but the harder omission is anyone who blanked while these three fired. The eleven picks itself once the benched men are counted, which is the whole indignity of the week.

And finally, a word about test31121, who managed to leave two of the best defensive returns in the division on his own bench and still find a third in Kostoulas up front. Owning the points is one thing. Playing them is another entirely.

stories.headline: Testing Times For The Nine-Point Pretenders
stories.deck: Four managers on nine points, but testf's 186 scored says the table is lying near the top
stories.body:
The table hands nine points to four sides and invites you to believe they are level. They are not. test211 sits top on 174 scored and a one-point squeak past 123, the kind of margin that flatters a decent side into looking like a great one. test2 has scored more than anyone above them and lost to test3 by 25, which tells you the record and the football have parted company.

Below the line the numbers turn mutinous. testf have posted 186, more than every side in the division, and sit fifth on six points, a haul with nothing to show for it. Meanwhile test31 grind out sixes on 136 scored and nobody is fooled. At the foot, test31121 lose by three and out-score two sides above them; the arithmetic is cruel, the football less so.

ranks.line: The best team in the league is fifth, and 186 scored is the only figure on this page that matters.
162 scored and a 25-point loss to show for it; the football says top three even if the beating says otherwise.
Put 25 on test2 and sit fourth, which is roughly a full division short of where that scoreline belongs.
Top of the table on a one-point win over a bottom-half side; flattered, and the 174 does not quite excuse it.
27 clear of test4 and nine points, but 164 scored is honest work rather than anything frightening.
165 scored and three points is a swindle; one point from top and treated like a relegation candidate.
145 and beaten by 27; the record is honest and so is the ceiling.
Six points off 136 scored is the lowest total of anyone above the drop; the wins are borrowed.
Bottom of the table, out-scoring two sides above them, undone by a three-point margin nobody will remember.
134 scored and beaten by 27; the only side down here whose record and football agree.

stories.headline: Davis Cup Sits Out On test4's Sofa
stories.deck: test4 benched Davis, who returned a goal and two assists in 90 minutes
stories.body:
The cruellest seat in the league belonged to Davis this week, planted on test4's bench while turning in a goal and two assists across the full ninety. A defender doing forward's work, and doing it for nobody who could count it.

test31121 managed the double insult. Yalcouyé took a goal and a clean sheet in 64 minutes, Gvardiol an assist and a clean sheet across the ninety, and both watched the round from the wrong side of the line. Two defenders working overtime, neither of them permitted to matter.

test211 left out Muharemović, who supplied an assist and kept his side tidy for ninety minutes. And 123, who saw Groß carry the load elsewhere, sat Donnarumma for a clean sheet and three saves. The goalkeeper did everything asked of him. Nobody asked.

stories.headline: Two In, One Out, Nobody Home
stories.deck: A quiet window: three deals across the league, David Raya dropped and left unclaimed.
stories.body:
Three moves, and the window barely creaked. test4 traded a man in for a man out and called it a day. test31 and testf each took one and gave back nothing. That is the week. No churn, no scramble, no queue at the door.

David Raya went out and stayed out. Signed in hope, dropped without ceremony, survived by a bench spot nobody has come to claim. He sits on the pile, gloves on, waiting for a phone that will not ring.

The men who might have moved did not, and the men who moved were few. When three deals is the whole of the league's business, there is no trend to trace, only the quiet of managers holding what they have and daring each other to blink first.

quiz.q: How many deals went through the window this week?
Which manager made a move both in and out?
Which two managers took one in and dropped nobody?
